Reconstructed on 2026-07-04 after file recovery. D. salina SA134 is a well-documented halophilic green alga with NaCl optimum ~2.5 M used for carotenoid production studies. Evidence source (PubMed 27020189) provides explicit salinity optimization data. NCBI Assembly GCA_002284615.2 (Dunsal1 v.2, JGI) is deposited under strain CCAP 19/18, which is an alias for SA134 in JGI/CCAP notation. Assembly has genbank_has_annotation confirmed. Strain identity caveat: SA134 (phenotype side) vs CCAP 19/18 (assembly side) should be verified as identical before downstream use.

G. sulphuraria Merola002 is a thermoacidophilic Cyanidiales alga with OGT ~42-45 C and pH optimum ~2.0, accepted here at ogt=45 C based on the strain-level evidence source (PubMed 34202768). RefSeq assembly GCF_000341285.1 (ASM34128v1, strain 074W, Galdieria sulphuraria Genome Project 2013) has full annotation confirmed (genbank_has_annotation, refseq_has_annotation). STRAIN MISMATCH: phenotype evidence is for Merola002 but the assembly is for strain 074W; these are distinct isolates and this entry is strain-adjacent. Verify identity before downstream use.

Reconstructed on 2026-07-04 after file recovery. N. oceanica CCAP849/10 is a marine microalga with best growth performance at ~25 ppt (~0.43 M NaCl), qualifying as saline-adapted. Evidence from PubMed 26528905 provides explicit salinity-growth data. NCBI Assembly GCA_037830525.2 (Noce_CCAP84910_1.0, Los Alamos National Laboratory, released 2025-11-19) is the exact-strain assembly for CCAP849/10 with annotation confirmed (genbank_has_annotation, has_annotation). Added during algae expansion pass on 2026-07-04. N. gaditana CCMP526 is a marine microalga with optimal growth at seawater-equivalent salinity (~35 ppt, ~0.60 M NaCl), qualifying as saline-adapted. RefSeq assembly GCF_000240725.1 was deposited alongside the original genome paper (Radakovits et al. 2012, Nature Communications) and is expected to carry annotated protein FASTA files. Phenotype evidence is based on the organism's marine ecology rather than an explicit measured salinity-optimum value; borderline saline-adapted classification. NCBI taxid 72520 should be verified against current NCBI Taxonomy.

Promoted from hold on 2026-07-05. Phenotype evidence from Fu et al. 2020 (Frontiers in Microbiology, DOI 10.3389/fmicb.2019.03005): G. partita strain THAL043 was cultivated at 40°C, pH 2.0 (MA medium) and was isolated from a stream at pH 2.15 and ambient temperature 46-48°C in the Tatun Volcano Group area, Taiwan. The 46-48°C isolation habitat constitutes evidence that OGT >= 45°C; lab cultivation at 40°C with pH 2.0 confirms acid-thermophilic growth. OGT stored as 45°C (conservative lower bound derived from habitat temperature). Multiple papers describe G. partita as thermophilic and thermoacidophilic. STRAIN CAVEAT: phenotype evidence is for THAL043 (Taiwan isolate) but genome assembly GCA_025991245.1 (GpartN1_1.0, NIG Japan 2022) is for strain NBRC 102759; these are distinct isolates of the same species. Collection match is therefore strain_adjacent, consistent with the G. sulphuraria precedent in this tracker. FTP: ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCA/025/991/245/GCA_025991245.1_GpartN1_1.0

Added 2026-07-05. Chlamydomonas sp. UWO 241 (strain UWO 241) is a well-characterised psychrophilic Antarctic green alga isolated from Lake Bonney, Antarctica. Zhang et al. 2021 (iScience 24:102084, DOI 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102084) is the draft genome paper; its Transparent Methods supplement (page 7, Strain and culture conditions) explicitly states: "UWO241 was cultured at 5°C" with continuous aeration in thermo-regulated aquaria. This is a culture temperature rather than a separately stated optimum growth temperature, but it constitutes strong primary-source evidence of psychrophilic cultivation conditions well below the <=15°C threshold. The NCBI BioProject PRJNA547753 title describes it as "Antarctic psychrophilic green alga"; Kalra et al. 2020 (Plant Physiol. 183:588-605) also explicitly calls it a "halotolerant psychrophile." STRAIN: single strain UWO 241 = alias UWO241 throughout the literature. Assembly GCA_016618255.1 (CUWO241_v1.0_nuclear, Scaffold, 65x, Western University 2021) has 16,018 protein-coding genes confirmed in NCBI Protein and FTP protein FASTA verified 200 OK on 2026-07-05. FTP: ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCA/016/618/255/GCA_016618255.1_CUWO241_v1.0_nuclear/GCA_016618255.1_CUWO241_v1.0_nuclear_protein.faa.gz

Added 2026-07-06. Galdieria yellowstonensis is a thermoacidophilic red alga formally described by Park et al. 2023 (J. Phycol. 59:444-466, DOI 10.1111/jpy.13322), which places it in the thermoacidophilic Galdieria lineage (order Galdieriales). SAG culture collection entry (SAG:108.79, https://sagdb.uni-goettingen.de/detailedList.php?str_number=108.79) explicitly states: "requires low pH (2-4) and prefers higher growth temperature (25°C, up to 55°C)." Kristijarti et al. 2024 (J. Appl. Phycol. 36:3199-3207, DOI 10.1007/s10811-024-03353-4) explicitly calls SAG 108.79 a "primitive photosynthetic thermoacidophile." Isolated from an acid (pH 3-4) hot spring in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming (collected 2017-06-02). Kristijarti et al. 2024 Materials and Methods explicitly states: "The Galdieria strains were grown in Allen medium (Allen 1959) at pH 2 with 3% glycerol (v/v) at 40°C, in the dark, and at 150 rpm" — this covers strain 108.79 directly and constitutes a primary-source cultivation temperature of 40°C at pH 2.0. The same paper's introduction states the genus has "adapted to grow at temperatures as high as 55°C." OGT stored as 45°C (conservative: explicit cultivation at 40°C + documented growth up to 55°C supports OGT in the 45-55°C range, consistent with thermoacidophilic classification; no standalone growth-optimum curve paper was found). pH optimum stored as 2.0 (explicit from Kristijarti 2024 cultivation conditions; SAG documents growth range pH 2-4). STRAIN: 108.79 E11 is the genome-sequenced sub-clone; SAG:108.79 is the culture-collection alias. FORMER NAMES: previously deposited in SAG as Cyanidium caldarium and Galdieria sulphuraria (Galdieri) Merola 1982; reassigned to G. yellowstonensis by Yoon, Park et McDermott 2023. Assembly GCA_026122205.1 (ASM2612220v1, Contig, 285x, Sungkyunkwan University 2022; annotation added 2024-01-05) has 7,022 protein-coding genes. FTP protein FASTA verified 200 OK on 2026-07-06. FTP: ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCA/026/122/205/GCA_026122205.1_ASM2612220v1/GCA_026122205.1_ASM2612220v1_protein.faa.gz

Added 2026-07-06. Polarella glacialis CCMP1383 is a psychrophilic Antarctic sea ice dinoflagellate (Dinophyceae, Alveolata) isolated from the ice edge at McMurdo Sound, Ross Sea, Antarctica in June 1991 (Montresor, Procaccini & Stoecker 1999, J. Phycol. 35:186-188). Stephens et al. 2020 (BMC Biology 18:57, PMID 32448240, PMC7245778) is the genome paper and explicitly describes P. glacialis as a 'psychrophilic (cold-adapted) free-living species,' with CCMP1383 as the Antarctic isolate from the Ross Sea and CCMP2088 as the complementary Arctic isolate from Baffin Bay. TEMPERATURE CAVEAT: no formal optimum growth temperature (OGT) from a dedicated growth-curve experiment was found. The NCMA culture collection record (https://ncma.bigelow.org/CCMP1383) lists Maintenance Temperature 2°C and Known Temperature Range 0-6°C; this constitutes explicit culture-temperature evidence from a citable primary culture collection, consistent with the <=15°C psychrophilic threshold. ogt_celsius is stored as 2 (NCMA maintenance temperature, not a formal measured OGT), following the same documentation convention used for Chlamydomonas sp. UWO 241 in this tracker. GENOME: GCA_905237085.1 (Pgla_CCMP1383, NCBI reference genome, Scaffold, University of Queensland 2021; BioProject PRJEB33539) has 58,229 protein-coding genes; annotation confirmed (genbank_has_annotation, has_annotation). Genome was generated from a single-cell amplified library. FTP protein FASTA verified 200 OK on 2026-07-06. LINEAGE NOTE: Polarella glacialis is the only dinoflagellate (Alveolata) in this tracker; it adds a completely new supergroup to the psychrophilic set alongside the existing Chlorophyta (C. subellipsoidea, UWO 241) and Bacillariophyta (F. cylindrus) psychrophiles.
